title: Which parity placements survive
claim: Exact on the frozen range: in the 8 harmonies with flip-blind triples, the not-all-equal stitch allows none (lemma A, a census). With each cell parity with probability rho (1/8 to 7/8), under 1% of placements survive for every n >= 6 and none of 11,497 samples at 7 x 7 to 9 x 9 (55 of 56 cells; cap). Neither frozen rule holds: class-level fit is not enough (705 placements), and one survivor class has an isolated parity cell. Over every survivor on 3 x 3 and 4 x 4, fixing from every base count: 10% from the parity equations alone, 14% with the harmony's states, 76% needs the not-all-equal stitches, 36% beyond arc consistency (on samples 38 / 25 / 37 / 25%). Referee pending.
failure_conditions: A fresh census that changes survival or the split of fixing.
Lemma A failing on one of the 8 harmonies.
remaining_obligations: Independent referee (the background referee thread): pending.
foundation_claim_scope: The plain not-all-equal law with flip-blind parity knots (A78); the 8 harmonies of period <= 16 with flip-blind triples; copies along two shifts on 3 x 3 and 4 x 4 (every placement) and to 9 x 9 (100 Bernoulli placements per harmony, size and rho; one cell cut by the cap).
